candidate.content: In ALFWorld pick-and-place tasks involving perishable food items (e.g., tomato), navigating directly to the semantically most likely container (fridge) before scanning other receptacles is a viable search strategy. However, if the target is not found in the high-probability container, the agent must fall back to systematic spatial scanning of remaining receptacles (cabinets, countertops, etc.) to locate the item.
candidate.scope: ALFWorld environments where the task requires acquiring a specific object (food item) and the room contains both semantic containers (fridge) and general storage surfaces. Applicable when the initial location of the target is unknown but semantic priors suggest a high probability for certain containers.

This semantic prioritization often yields faster acquisition than arbitrary spatial ordering or exhaustive type grouping.

probe_summary.realization_pattern: Semantic-prior-first traversal: select the single most probable container type based on object properties, then fall back to standard scan.
